claim: AWS recommends Multi-AZ file systems for most production workloads, and describes Single-AZ as a cost-efficient solution for test and development workloads and for production workloads with replication in the application layer or relaxed availability and RPO needs.
question: When should you choose Single-AZ or Multi-AZ for FSx for Windows File Server?

values.display: Multi-AZ file systems for most production workloads
cost-efficient solution for test and development workloads

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server deployment types

evidence.quote: We recommend using Multi-AZ file systems for most production workloads given the high availability and durability model it provides.

Single-AZ deployment is designed as a cost-efficient solution for test and development workloads, certain production workloads that have replication built into the application layer and do not require additional storage-level redundancy, and production workloads that have relaxed availability and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) needs.

claim: A Multi-AZ FSx for Windows file system fails over automatically from the preferred to the standby file server when an Availability Zone outage occurs, when the preferred file server becomes unavailable, or when it undergoes planned maintenance.
question: What triggers failover of a Multi-AZ FSx for Windows file system?

values.display: The preferred file server becomes unavailable

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ

evidence.quote: Multi-AZ file systems automatically fail over from the preferred file server to the standby file server if any of the following conditions occur:
An Availability Zone outage occurs.
The preferred file server becomes unavailable.
The preferred file server undergoes planned maintenance.

claim: A failover of a Multi-AZ FSx for Windows file system typically completes in less than 30 seconds, and failback to the preferred file server is automatic and also takes less than 30 seconds once the preferred file server has recovered.
question: How long does an FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ failover take?

values.display: promotion of the standby file server

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ

evidence.quote: A failover typically completes in less than 30 seconds from the detection of the failure on the active file server to the promotion of the standby file server to active status. Failback to the original Multi-AZ configuration also completes in less than 30 seconds, and only occurs once the file server in the preferred subnet is fully recovered.

claim: Because the file system's DNS name stays the same, failovers are transparent to Windows applications, which resume file system operations without manual intervention.
question: Do Windows applications need changes after an FSx for Windows File Server failover?

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ

evidence.quote: Because the file system's DNS name remains the same, failovers are transparent to Windows applications, which resume file system operations without manual intervention.

claim: Linux clients do not support automatic DNS-based failover, so they do not connect to the standby file server during a failover; they resume after the file system fails back to the preferred file server.
question: How do Linux clients behave during a Multi-AZ FSx for Windows failover?

values.display: do not support automatic DNS-based failover

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ

evidence.quote: Linux clients do not support automatic DNS-based failover. Therefore, they don't automatically connect to the standby file server during a failover. They will automatically resume file system operations after the Multi-AZ file system has failed back to the file server in the preferred subnet.

claim: While a Multi-AZ file system fails over and back, I/O may be paused and CloudWatch metrics may be temporarily unavailable, and synchronizing activity during that time can take up to multiple hours for HDD storage and for write-heavy, IOPS-heavy workloads.
question: What happens to I/O during failover of an FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system?

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ

evidence.quote: During the brief period in which your file system is failing over and failing back, I/O may be paused and Amazon CloudWatch metrics may be temporarily unavailable.

claim: FSx for Windows File Server backups are file-system-consistent (using VSS), highly durable and incremental, and Amazon FSx stores them in Amazon S3.
question: How are FSx for Windows File Server backups made consistent and stored?

values.display: stores backups in Amazon Simple Storage Service

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server backups

evidence.quote: With Amazon FSx, backups are file-system-consistent, highly durable, and incremental.

To ensure file system consistency, Amazon FSx uses the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) in Microsoft Windows. To ensure high durability, Amazon FSx stores backups in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).

claim: Amazon FSx takes an automatic daily backup by default; the default retention period is 30 days in the console and differs in the API and CLI, you can set it between 0 and 90 days, and 0 days turns automatic backups off.
question: What is the default retention of FSx for Windows File Server automatic daily backups?

values.display: automatic daily backup retention period is 30 days

qualifiers.scope: FSx for Windows File Server backups

evidence.quote: By default, Amazon FSx takes an automatic daily backup of your file system.

When you create a file system in the Amazon FSx console, the default automatic daily backup retention period is 30 days. The default retention period is different in the Amazon FSx API and CLI. You can set the retention period to be between 0–90 days. Setting the retention period to 0 (zero) days turns off automatic daily backups.

claim: User-initiated FSx for Windows File Server backups never expire, are kept even after the file system is deleted, and are deleted only by you.

evidence.quote: Your user-initiated backups of Amazon FSx file systems never expire, and they are available for as long as you want to keep them. User-initiated backups are retained even after you delete the file system that was backed up.

claim: Automatic daily backups of an FSx for Windows File Server file system are deleted when the file system is deleted.
